subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should persisted per-session `/exec` fields be allowed to override later stricter global or agent exec security config after a Discord session resumes?
rationale: The source reproduction is clear, but current docs and tests also encode `/exec` as durable session defaults, so changing it is a security-boundary and compatibility decision rather than a purely mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Make operator policy the upper bound
options.body: Clamp or clear stored session exec fields when they exceed current global or agent policy, with focused migration/reset coverage for existing entries.

options.title: Keep durable session defaults
options.body: Document that operators must reset or patch sessions to enforce later exec-policy changes for existing lanes.

options.title: Ship reset tooling first
options.body: Add an operator-facing session exec reset or doctor repair before changing precedence semantics for active sessions.

recommendation.title: Make operator policy the upper bound
recommendation.body: Clamp or clear stored session exec fields when they exceed current global or agent policy, with focused migration/reset coverage for existing entries.

likelyOwner.reason: The clearest history trail for the `/exec` session override behavior and resolver coverage points to this owner path.
